newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam calls Deng's death a loss for China.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam calls Deng's death a loss for China.

text.p: Vietnam's top leaders, in their first comment on the death of a man once considered a mortal enemy, have sent a message to Beijing describing the death of Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday as a loss for China.

The statement, carried in Friday's official press, expressed sympathy and said Deng had made important contributions to the development of the People's Republic of China and to its ecomomic and social opening.
"The death of Comrade Deng Xiaoping is a great loss to the Communist Party and the people of China," the statement said.
But there was no mention of his role in relations between the two socialist neighbours, who fought a 1979 border war which was followed by a lengthy period of frontier hostilities.
Deng is viewed by historians as the man responsible for that war, launched to punish Vietnam for its late 1978 invasion of Cambodia.
Relations between the two neighbours were normalised in 1991.
Hanoi, which has previously held periods of official mourning for socialist leaders of Deng's stature, has yet to announce a similar measure.
The statement also expressed hope Deng's reforms would continue under his heir apparent President Jiang Zemin.

"It is our belief that under the leadership of the CPC with respected Comrade General Secretary Jiang Zemin as the nucleus, the communists and people of China will overcome their grief to persist in the line of reforms and opening up to build a prosperous and modern China along the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, thus making a worthy contribution to the cause of peace, stability and development in the region and world."
